events.text:
New day, new job:

This is a new `Tracker:` PR.



First we need to set up the Gen-3 material mapping for the nODD Tracker, using the 100k geantinos in the storage directory.



As a first step:

- make a r-z scatter plot where the Geant material is located
- overlay this with the portal surfaces of the Gen3 Tracker geometry
- suggest a set of surfaces where the material should be mapped onto with the following objectives:
  - if pixel sensor points inwards and most of the material is behind the sensitive sensor, map to the closest surface afterwards
  - otherwise map to the closest surface before
  - if there is junk of material where there's no surface close by flag this

I’ll inspect the recorded material positions and Gen3 geometry, then build an r–z overlay and a proposed mapping assignment that respects each sensor’s orientation. I’ll also flag material clusters without a nearby suitable surface and package this first step in a new `Tracker:` PR.

I’m using the acts-spack skill to verify the runtime and the repository’s nODD coordination workflow for this new mapping study. I’ll keep it as a first-step proposal: plots, candidate mapping surfaces and explicit flags for material that doesn’t fit the proposed assignment.

The scan is still available and PR #99 is merged. The environment registry still reports stale fingerprints and no staged DD4hep/Geant4 source trees, so I’ll verify the installed runtime directly. The first mapping study can use the existing ACTS source and installed headers without changing shared dependencies.

The new branch starts from merged PR #99. I’m checking the native Gen3 portals and sensor orientations so the proposed “before” and “after” surfaces follow the geantino flight direction. I’ll report the distance criterion used to flag material that has no nearby carrier.

The geometry source defines pixel local `+w` as pointing toward the support. The barrel support direction is outward, so those sensors face inward. Endcap discs have modules on both faces, so their mapping proposal needs to preserve that distinction rather than choose one side for the whole disc.

The full classification finished: all 100,000 tracks and 17,137,021 material steps were matched, with zero missing labels or density mismatches. I’ll keep native sensor and beam-pipe material in place and survey the passive tracker material for portal mapping, avoiding double counting in a later material map.

The native export has 121 unique portal surfaces across 117 tracking volumes. All 45,646 sensor frames agree with the detector report. I’m now measuring distances using the full recording; the scatter view will show a deterministic sample, while the budgets and material flags will use every step.

The existing portals are too far from much of the service material: with a provisional 10 mm criterion, 62.6% of the recorded passive tracker X₀ lies beyond every portal. For rays with an identified pixel crossing, 83–85% of barrel backing X₀ is downstream, supporting the “after” rule; endcap inward faces show about 91%. I’m flagging the remote services for additional carrier surfaces.

The proposal now lists the nearby native carrier IDs by layer and flags 33 connected remote-material clusters. The largest gaps are in pixel, short-strip and long-strip service routes. I’ll include the exact component paths behind those broad clusters, then get an independent physics-validation review before opening the PR.

The figures and surface tables are ready, and all 14 portable controls pass. The original 54 material profiles are unchanged. The independent reviewer has found no blocking issue so far and is finishing the scan/provenance checks; I’m preparing the PR with the service gaps and unresolved pixel associations stated explicitly.
The GitHub connector can’t create this PR with its current permissions. I’ll use the authenticated GitHub CLI to open it from the pushed branch.

[PR #100](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/100) is open. The reviewer independently recomputed the finite-portal distances for all 100,000 tracks and reproduced the remote-material counts at 5, 10 and 20 mm exactly. I’m finishing the discussion and usage records, then rerunning the PR checks with those records included.

pull_request.head: codex/tracker-gen3-material-mapping
pull_request.body:
Add the first Gen3 material-mapping survey from the existing 100k-geantino recording: an r–z material scatter with the actual native portals, pixel orientation/behind-sensor diagnostics, and finite before/after carrier suggestions. Keep native sensor and beam-pipe material separate.

The full 17,137,021-step survey flags 33 remote-material clusters. At a provisional 10 mm spatial criterion, 62.6% of passive tracker X₀ is remote from every existing portal, so the proposal explicitly calls for additional service carriers. Unmatched pixel sensor associations remain visible; no material map or geometry change is installed.

- [Figures, proposed native carrier IDs and limitations](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/tracker-gen3-material-mapping/docs/validation/gen3-material-mapping/README.md)
- [Reproduction commands](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/tracker-gen3-material-mapping/software/analysis/gen3_material_mapping/README.md)
- Validation: full native export/round trip, all-step labels and budget closure, 14 finite-geometry/rule controls, exact preservation of all 54 prior profiles, and portable figure/table replay. Hosted CI adds the replay.
- Discussion, specialist handoffs and exact closed-turn usage are recorded in SESSION-2026-10-26-gen3-material-mapping. Active parent usage is excluded until its turn closes.

DRAFT scientific proposal under DES-024/025; material-map closure, binning convergence and tracking validation remain future work.

events.text:
**GEN3MAP-PhysVal-01 — independent review complete**

Reviewed revision: `a99b63cba68f8c66723df6ed5c55935e6675971a`. Read-only; no files changed. No blocking defects found for the requested **first-step plots and surface proposal**. This is not detector acceptance or validation of a finished map.

Findings requiring follow-up before production mapping:

- **Medium:** 968,999 passive pixel steps lack a same-ray, same-layer sensitive crossing and carry **76.21% of pixel passive X₀**. Their provisional before assignment cannot establish sensor-facing order. This is accurately disclosed in `docs/validation/gen3-material-mapping/README.md:127` and implemented at `survey.py:194–226`.
- **Medium:** Choosing a finite portal before/after the material midpoint does not establish preservation of order relative to intervening sensitive planes, especially shared two-face backing. The report explicitly retains this limitation at `README.md:135–140`; ownership and segmentation remain necessary.
- **Low:** The recording’s geometry revision, seed and original command are unavailable. Matching compact/factory hashes and density checks support the selected comparison geometry but cannot establish its identity with the recording geometry. The report states this correctly at `README.md:142–154`.

Actual checks:

- **14 portable tests passed**, executing exact target-commit source retrieved with `git show`.
- Independently streamed **all 100,000 tracks / 17,137,021 steps** using closed-form distances to finite cylinders/annuli rather than the implementation’s segment projection. Exact remote counts at **5 / 10 / 20 mm** matched: **3,654,429 / 962,351 / 376,735**. Passive X₀ fractions matched **78.2652% / 62.5766% / 46.7871%**.
- Recomputed full component counts, passive mean **1.1241328378816744 X₀**, and per-track X₀/λI closure.
- Replayed the first 5,000 tracks’ raw midpoint coordinates, scatter categories and remote flags exactly.
- Verified input hashes for recording, labels, classification and native export; committed portal/volume catalogues equal the hashed native export.
- Verified budget/count partitions, cluster/region totals, **118 candidate portals / 101 nearby**, and **121 unique nonzero ACTS geometry IDs**.
- Inspected pinned recorder source: positions are pre-step coordinates, confirming the midpoint correction. Inspected native adapter/factories: +w is support-facing; native silicon slabs and the Be cylinder are retained separately.
- Visually inspected three pinned PNGs; legends, portal overlay and remote-region locators are readable.

The strict downstream-majority rule and finite directional selection are supported by code and retained evidence. The provisional 10 mm criterion is clearly labeled and accompanied by threshold sensitivity. No new native export, simulation, material-map replay or reconstruction validation was run. The coordinator’s later portable CSV exporter is outside this pinned assessment.
